body.statement: With probability \(1-o(1)\) over \(G_n\), the procedure \((\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}},\widehat\tau_G)\) satisfies \[\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\mathbb E[(\widehat\tau_G-\tau_G)^2\mid G]\le C r(n,d).\] Moreover, the full-GATE conflict graph obeys \(\lambda(H_G)=\Theta(d^2)\) on the same graph event, so this guarantee is smaller by a factor of order \(\log(d+2)\) than the published \(O(\lambda(H_G)/n)=O(d^2/n)\) conflict-graph-design guarantee.
body.justification: This converts the covariance kernel into the first full two-sided procedure at the logarithmic lower-edge scale.
body.gap: Kandiros, Pipis, Daskalakis, and Harshaw give \(O(d^2/n)\) here, while Li and Li's sharper construction covers only the treated component.
body.consumer: Experimenters obtain the sample-size law \(n\gg d^2/\log d\) for vanishing worst-case GATE error rather than the sufficient law \(n\gg d^2\).

obligation.what_is_open: Close the risk upper bound without presuming the unresolved operator estimate in \(\text{thm:stable-kernel}\).
obligation.obstruction: The exact risk identity reduces the theorem to \(\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}=O(n/k)\).  That is precisely the unresolved novel kernel assertion, so the logarithmic gain cannot be obtained from the current frozen primitives.
obligation.attempted: I derived the risk implication equation by equation and separately verified the \(\Theta(d^2)\) conflict-graph spectral comparison.  Replacing operator control by an entrywise or maximum-row-sum bound loses the factor \(\log(d+2)\).
obligation.partial_result:
On the event asserted by \(\text{thm:stable-kernel}\), \(\text{lem:exact-risk-certificate}\) gives immediately
\[
\sup_{y\in\mathcal M_2(G)}\operatorname{MSE}(\widehat\tau_G\mid G)
\le \frac{2\|\Gamma_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}}{n}
\le C\frac{(d+1)^2}{n\log(d+2)}=Cr(n,d).
\]
Independently, if \(B_G\) is the \(V\times V\) zero--one matrix of the relation \(\operatorname{dist}_G(i,j)\le2\), then the adjacency matrix of \(H_G\) is \(\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&B_G\\B_G&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)\), so \(\lambda(H_G)=\|B_G\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Every row sum is at most \(1+d^2\).  Under \(d=o(\sqrt n)\), the expected number of collisions among the \(d(d-1)\) length-two walks from a uniform vertex is \(O(d^4/n+d^2/n)=o(d^2)\); Markov's inequality shows that the average row sum is \((1-o_{\Pr}(1))d^2\).  The Rayleigh quotient at the all-ones vector and the maximum-row-sum bound then give \(\lambda(H_G)=\Theta_{\Pr}(d^2)\).  Hence only the unresolved covariance-kernel estimate prevents the full target proof.
